committees.name: Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee

dimensions.assessment: Affects state, local, tribal, territorial governments, private sector partners, fusion centers, and DHS intelligence personnel.
dimensions.evidence: State, local, Tribal, and territorial governments and private sector entities

dimensions.assessment: Shifts operational priorities and resource allocation within a federal intelligence office to emphasize two-way information sharing and regional partnerships.
dimensions.evidence: operational mission of providing timely and efficient intelligence support to State, local, Tribal, and territorial governments and private sector entities is sufficiently prioritized and resourced

dimensions.assessment: Directs organizational realignment within existing resources, requiring a report to Congress without stating new federal appropriations.
dimensions.evidence: Any resource or organizational changes to the Office required to sustain such realignment.

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to add specific statutory mandates for the Office of Intelligence and Analysis.
dimensions.evidence: To amend the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to realign the mission of the Office of Intelligence and Analysis

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory realignment of the office's mission, accompanied by a one-time reporting requirement within 180 days.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Under Secretary... shall submit... a report

missing_information: Specific budget reallocations or staffing numbers shifted to support the mission realignment
Quantitative metrics currently used by the office
importance_detail.rationale: Realigns the mission of the Department of Homeland Security's Office of Intelligence and Analysis to prioritize support for state, local, tribal, territorial governments, and private sector entities equally with federal intelligence elements.
